- Brent crude has meanwhile moved to over $83 a barrel after Yemen’s Iran-linked Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia, further escalating tensions in the Middle East.
- Gold has meanwhile maintained its recovery, moving up 1.5% to now trade at $4,300 per ounce as investors move toward safety in the face of uncertainty.
Bitcoin is holding near $64,700 Friday, barely changed over the last 24-hour period, while the broader CoinDesk 20 (CD20) index is down 0.2% over the period.
Brent crude has meanwhile moved to over $83 a barrel after Yemen’s Iran-linked Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia, further escalating tensions in the Middle East.
Treasury yields have seen a slight correction, but remain at 4.67% for the 10-year note, a level Fidelity’s Director of Global Macro Jurrien Timmer said “history suggests that nothing good happens.”
Higher oil could add to inflation pressure if sustained, while elevated Treasury yields tighten financial conditions. Together, they could limit expectations for near-term rate cuts and weigh on bitcoin and other risk assets.
Gold has meanwhile maintained its recovery, moving up 1.5% to now trade at $4,300 per ounce as investors move toward safety in the face of uncertainty.
Derivatives positioning
- Long-short taker ratio: The crypto futures market’s long-short taker ratio has returned to neutral after leaning bullish on Thursday, suggesting traders may be adopting a more cautious stance ahead of the U.S. payrolls report.
- CC token leads OI growth: Canton Network’s CC token is down 13% in 24 hours, yet its futures open interest (OI) has surged over 5%. The combination is said to validate the downtrend, especially as the 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta remains negative, indicating sellers are more aggressive by shorting futures via market orders rather than passive limit orders.
- Open Interest Movers: DOGE, XRP, and SUI are open interest gainers, while SHIB has seen a drop.
- CVD Indicator: The CVD indicator paints a bearish picture for the market, as most majors (excluding ADA, HBAR, and ETH) show negative CVD readings.
- Volatility Indexes: The BVIV index, representing BTC’s annualized 30-day implied volatility, remains near a long-held floor of 36%, showing little signs of stress despite the Clarity Act delay and the impending U.S. jobs report. The same holds true for ether’s volatility index (EVIV).
- Options Activity: In Deribit-listed options, puts (bearish bets) at the $60,000 and $62,000 strikes dominate the 24-hour volume rankings for BTC, while the $2,000 call is the most popular for ETH.
Token Talk
- Sui is adding quantum-resistant security to its accounts, integrating two post-quantum signature schemes approved by the U.S. standards body NIST, per The Block. The upgrade lets users optionally adopt quantum-safe keys derived from their existing recovery phrases, so nobody has to generate a new seed or move funds to a new address to be protected.
- The threat it's guarding against is specific to crypto. In most systems an attacker has to break in before they can go after a key. Onchain, the public key is exposed permanently the moment an account transacts, which opens the door to "harvest-now, forge-later," where attackers collect exposed keys today and crack them once quantum computers are capable enough to run Shor's algorithm, the technique that could break the elliptic-curve cryptography securing most wallets. No quantum hardware is needed to start collecting.
- Sui is using two schemes for two risk levels. ML-DSA-65 covers everyday accounts at the protocol level, and the hash-based SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s runs inside Move smart contracts for high-value vaults. The two rest on different math, so a weakness in one doesn't compromise the other. Sui went with a higher security tier after a July incident where an AI model halved the effective strength of a different post-quantum candidate, a reason to carry margin rather than pick the cheapest option.
- It's a feature add, not a rebuild. Sui says it was built for "cryptographic agility," meaning new signature schemes slot in without touching consensus or existing balances, so this ships as a routine protocol update. That contrasts with bitcoin and ethereum, where quantum-proofing is a heavier lift, and lands the same month Strategy and BlackRock formed a consortium to prepare bitcoin for the same threat. title: Coldcard fallout shows up onchain as 210,000 bitcoin leaves old wallets
full_text:
Coldcard fallout shows up onchain as 210,000 bitcoin leaves old wallets
Roughly 200,000 bitcoin have moved from long-term holder wallets in the past week, suggesting a possible shift in custody rather than conventional selling
- Long-term holder supply has fallen by roughly 210,000 bitcoin, from nearly 15 million BTC to approximately 14.7 million BTC.
- The movement comes with bitcoin almost 50% below its record high, unlike previous distribution waves near market peaks.
- The movement is linked to the Coldcard incident, with users transferring bitcoin to newly generated wallets or regulated custody services.
The fallout from the Coldcard security breach is now surfacing on-chain.
According to Glassnode data, roughly 210,000 BTC have moved out of long-term holder (LTH) wallets over the past week, the largest decline since December 2024, when bitcoin approached $100,000 for the first time.
Glassnode classifies long-term holders, or LTHs, as entities whose coins have remained dormant for approximately 155 days, or just over five months. This cohort is often considered the market’s “smart money” because its members tend to hold through short-term volatility.
Long-term holder supply now stands at approximately 14.7 million BTC. Before the Coldcard incident, it was just under 15 million BTC, close to an all-time high.
Historically, heavy spending by long-term holders has coincided with periods of market strength or tops. Similar waves of distribution occurred around the market peaks of March 2021, March 2024 and December 2024, as experienced holders took profits into rising demand.
This time, however, the movement is occurring near the lows. Bitcoin is trading around $64,000, roughly 50% below its October all-time high.
This type of spending from this cohort is not profit-taking, but a migration in how bitcoin is being stored following the Coldcard incident. In addition, bitcoin did not make new lows following the hack.
The breach stemmed from weak randomness in affected Coldcard firmware, which allowed attackers to reconstruct some users’ wallet recovery phrases and drain their bitcoin. Thousands of addresses were affected, with estimated losses reaching as much as $114 million. Coldcard subsequently urged affected users to generate new wallets and move their funds because updating the firmware alone cannot secure keys that may already be compromised, according to CoinDesk.
Some of the decline in long-term holder supply could therefore reflect users transferring bitcoin into newly generated wallets with stronger custody arrangements. Other holders may be moving their assets to regulated custodians or spot bitcoin ETFs as they reconsider the risks of self-custody.
ETF flows offer some support, U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs attracted approximately $754 million over the past week, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), accounting for most of those inflows.
The crucial distinction is that on-chain movement does not necessarily mean selling. In this case, the decline in long-term holder supply may be capturing a broader migration in bitcoin custody rather than a straightforward loss of conviction.

title: CleanSpark misses Wall Street revenue estimates as shares sink

CleanSpark misses Wall Street revenue estimates as shares sink
CleanSpark’s shares fell 5.5% on Thursday after the Bitcoin miner reported $138 million in quarterly revenue, narrowly missing Wall Street’s consensus estimate.
Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin mining company CleanSpark reported $138 million in revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
The $138 million represented a 30.5% year-over-year decrease from $198 million, according to its quarterly results published on Thursday.
CleanSpark also reported a net loss of $239 million, or $0.89 per basic share, for the three months ended on June 30, compared with $257 million in net income, or $0.90 per share, for the same period last year.
The revenue narrowly missed analysts’ consensus estimate of $142.2 million, according to analyst estimates compiled by Yahoo Finance.
CleanSpark’s shares fell 5.5% on Thursday, but staged a 3% pre-market recovery on Friday to trade above $13.10, Yahoo Finance data showed.
CleanSpark is among the companies that have expanded beyond their core Bitcoin (BTC) mining operations into AI and high-performance computing infrastructure.
On July 14, CleanSpark signed a 20-year data center lease with an undisclosed investment-grade global technology company for a 175-megawatt data center at its Sandersville, Georgia, campus. The company estimated the deal would generate $6.6 billion in contracted revenue over the initial term.

title: Stripe-owned Bridge joins EU MiCA register after Luxembourg approval
summary: Stripe-owned Bridge has entered the EU MiCA register following Luxembourg approval, joining regulated providers under the bloc’s crypto framework.
full_text:
Stripe-owned Bridge joins EU MiCA register after Luxembourg approval
Stripe-owned Bridge has entered the EU MiCA register following Luxembourg approval, joining regulated providers under the bloc’s crypto framework.
Bridge Building, the Luxembourg-based entity behind Stripe-owned stablecoin infrastructure company Bridge, has joined the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register after receiving regulatory approval in Luxembourg.
Bridge’s inclusion brings the number of MiCA-authorized electronic money token (EMT) issuers in the EU register to 42, according to the latest European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) update published on Wednesday.
The addition came weeks after Bridge announced on July 2 that it had secured a Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorization under MiCA and an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence from Luxembourg’s Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier. Bridge’s Head of Product, Mai Leduc Blount, said the approvals allow businesses in the EU to build stablecoin and payment products under a regulated framework.
The same ESMA update added three new CASP entries from Germany, including Volksbank Die Gestalterbank, VBU Volksbank im Unterland and VR-Bank Erding, bringing the total number of authorized CASPs in the EU register to 324.
The update showed no changes to asset-referenced token authorizations, with no ART issuers listed. The list of non-compliant crypto asset companies was also unchanged.
ESMA has published more frequent updates to its MiCA register in recent weeks, with several updates in July.

title: ‘Applesauce’: Michigan judge denies Coinbase bid to block state enforcement of sports event contracts
summary: "Coinbase's averments are, in a word, applesauce," U.S. District Judge Shalina Kumar wrote in Thursday's ruling.
full_text:
'Applesauce': Michigan judge denies Coinbase bid to block state enforcement of sports event contracts
Quick Take
- A Michigan federal judge has rejected Coinbase’s preliminary injunction motion seeking to block potential state enforcement over its planned offering of sports event contracts.
- “Coinbase’s averments are, in a word, applesauce,” U.S. District Judge Shalina Kumar wrote in the ruling.
We'd love your feedback.
A Michigan federal judge has denied Coinbase's preliminary injunction bid to block state enforcement against sports event contracts.
U.S. District Judge Shalina Kumar of the Eastern District of Michigan ruled on Thursday that Coinbase failed to establish that it is likely to succeed on the merits of its claims that federal law preempts Michigan's jurisdiction.
The crypto exchange sued Michigan in December 2025, arguing that prediction markets fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission under the federal Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) rather than state gaming regulators.
Coinbase specifically seeks to use its platform to provide customers, including those in Michigan, access to event contracts offered by Kalshi.
The exchange claims that Michigan's gambling laws are "conflict preempted" because they frustrate Congress's efforts to create a uniform federal regulatory scheme and because complying with both the CEA and the state's Lawful Sports Betting Act (LSBA) would be impossible, according to the filing.
However, the judge rejected the arguments, holding that Coinbase failed to show that sports event contracts qualify as swaps under the CEA. She also rejected the exchange's contention that complying with both federal and state law would be impossible.
"Coinbase's averments are, in a word, applesauce," Judge Kumar wrote. "[It] is not impossible for Coinbase to comply with the LSBA simply because it is costly and challenging."
"Coinbase has not carried its burden to establish the factors required for a preliminary injunction against the Defendants," the judge added.
The Block has reached out to Coinbase for comment.
Nationwide battle
The Michigan case is part of a broader legal battle over prediction markets regulation. In December, Coinbase sued the states of Michigan, Illinois, and Connecticut, intensifying an ongoing legal dispute.
"State efforts to control or outright block these markets stifle innovation and violate the law," Coinbase Chief Legal Officer Paul Grewal said at the time.
"Prediction markets are fundamentally different from sportsbooks," Grewal added. "Casinos win only if you lose and set odds to maximize their profits. Prediction markets are neutral exchanges, indifferent to price, that match buyers and sellers."
The CFTC has also sued several states as part of its push to establish federal oversight of the industry. In June, Kentucky became the ninth state to be sued by the CFTC. Over the past year, the agency has brought complaints against Wisconsin, Illinois, Arizona, Connecticut, New York, New Mexico, Minnesota, and Rhode Island.
Also in June, the CFTC unveiled a slate of new rules that would still allow overall support for sports betting, despite opposition from state regulators.

title: MyTrade Founder Fined $10K Over Bots That Wash Traded 60 Cryptocurrencies
summary: Liu Zhou told undercover agents the objective was to make other buyers lose money, according to the Justice Department.
full_text:
In brief
- MyTrade founder Liu Zhou has been fined $10,000 over running a crypto wash trading service.
- Zhou pleaded guilty in October 2024 alongside 17 co-conspirators charged in the same operation.
- MyTrade's dashboard let clients order a daily volume of fake trades, executed by bots.
The founder of crypto market maker MyTrade has avoided prison and been fined $10,000 for running a wash trading service that generated millions of dollars in fake daily volume across roughly 60 cryptocurrencies.
Liu Zhou, 41, a Canadian citizen and Chinese national, was sentenced in Boston federal court on Thursday by U.S. District Judge Angel Kelley, who imposed no custodial term, Law360 reported. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit market manipulation and wire fraud after being charged in October 2024 alongside 17 other individuals and entities.
MyTrade sold the service openly. Clients logged into a dashboard on the MyTrade MM website and specified how many wash trades they wanted executed each day on named exchanges, a product the firm called "Volume Support." Bots did the rest, buying and selling the same asset repeatedly to inflate apparent volume. As of October 2024 the service had dozens of clients.
Zhou was candid with people he believed were prospective customers. MyTrade MM "does self-trades — a buy and a sell in the same second," he told them, and its volume bot could be used to run pump and dumps. The point, he said, was to draw in "other buyers from the community, people you don't know about or don't care about," because "we have to make [the other buyers] lose money in order to make profit."
The FBI built its own token
Investigators created NexFundAI, a fictitious crypto company complete with a website and an Ethereum-based token that traded on Uniswap until law enforcement disabled it, then used it to solicit market-making services and record what was offered.
The sting produced charges against 18 individuals and entities in October 2024, including market makers Gotbit, ZM Quant and CLS Global.
Zhou's plea agreement required MyTrade MM to stop selling Volume Support and permanently deactivate the bots behind it. It also required the firm to post a notice on its own website stating that volume support is "a form of wash trading and illegal under the laws of the United States."

title: Senate Punts Clarity Act Vote to September as Democrats Hold Out
summary: Senate Majority Leader Thune says the bill will be queued up when lawmakers return, leaving weeks to find 60 votes before midterms take over.
full_text:
In brief
- The Senate leaves for a month-long recess without holding a procedural vote on the Clarity Act.
- Republicans need roughly six Democratic crossovers to clear the 60-vote threshold.
- If it passes the Senate, the bill returns to the House before it can reach Trump's desk.
The U.S. Senate will not vote on the Clarity Act before its August recess, pushing the crypto market structure bill to September and into the closing weeks before midterm campaigning consumes the calendar.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) confirmed the delay late Thursday. "The Dems are insistent on no Clarity vote," he said in remarks posted by his press office, adding that he had worked with the bill's sponsors and that Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) "was great, and we're getting that queued up first thing when we come back."
.@LeaderJohnThune announces Clarity will be on the floor in September:
“The Dems are insistent on no Clarity vote... I worked with sponsors of the bill. @SenLummis was great, and we’re getting that queued up first thing when we come back.”
— Stacey Daniels (@staceydanielsDC) August 7, 2026
The chamber leaves Friday and returns in mid-September for a few weeks before attention shifts to November's elections, making that window the last realistic one this year. A source familiar with the matter told The Block that Senate Democrats were reluctant to vote ahead of the midterms given the crypto industry's growing political influence, and that the delay buys time to assemble the 60 votes needed.
That math has not changed since the bill cleared the Senate Banking Committee 15-9 in May, when only two Democrats crossed, Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD). Roughly six are needed on the floor. Republican support has also wavered. Should the bill clear the Senate, it would return to the House for another vote before reaching President Donald Trump.
Ethics remains the roadblock
The sticking points are the same ones that have dogged the bill all year: stablecoin rewards, whether the bill arms law enforcement adequately against illicit finance, and above all the ethics provisions covering Trump's own crypto holdings.
Those provisions could pay him. An addendum negotiated by Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC) and Gallego, still unreleased and being worked out with the White House, would require the president to divest from crypto-related businesses. Forced divestiture would also let him defer federal capital gains tax on those holdings, potentially for years, Bloomberg reported, and if he held the replacement investments until death the gains would escape tax entirely.
Trump reported $1.4 billion in crypto and meme coin earnings for 2025, and holds a 38% stake in World Liberty Financial through an affiliated company. Without deferral he would face a 20% rate. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have both used the same provision on their own divestments.
The addendum would also let state attorneys general sue to enforce the ethics measures where the Justice Department declines to. Whether Trump accepts it is unresolved.
Decrypt reported two weeks ago that the bill was on the ropes, with Thune already signalling it would not clear the chamber before the break. Galaxy Research cut its odds of passage this year to a coin toss in June.
Industry groups struck a determined tone, with Crypto Council for Innovation CEO Ji Hun Kim noting the postponement was disappointing but the direction unchanged. Every day without a framework "pushes American users and builders offshore and leaves consumers at risk," Kim said in a statement.
There is a fallback should the Clarity Act falter. SEC Chair Paul Atkins said last month the agency is ready to write crypto rules itself if the legislation stalls, an outcome the industry has resisted because regulation by rulemaking can be undone by the next administration.

title: Can the Polestar 3 save you from hay fever?
summary: Plus four more ways to clear the air for allergy sufferers
full_text:
Can the Polestar 3 save you from hay fever?
Simply sign up to the Technology myFT Digest -- delivered directly to your inbox.
Health drive
I’d never seen the words “mugwort” or “ragweed” on the digital display of a car before, let alone details of whether either plant had recently ejected pollen in the vicinity. A summer morning in the all-electric Polestar 3 changed all that. As it happens, ragweed posed no threat that day, but the same could not be said for mugwort, and for those like me who sneeze at its very mention, this premium SUV ended up being a sensible place to hang out.
Most reviews of modern cars inevitably concentrate on air suspension or battery efficiency, and that’s as it should be, but the Polestar 3 is also a supremely effective banisher of troublesome particles, dust and pollen, making its cabin something of a sanctuary. “Advanced Air Cleaning” – which is always active unless you’ve manually turned off ventilation or recirculation – swaps out all 3,000 litres of cabin air every minute, replacing it with new stuff while filtering out 95 per cent of harmful particles (down to 2.5 micrometres), 97 per cent of viruses and 99.9 per cent of pollen. Achieving what it calls “CleanZone” is its aim, and the current state of play is depicted on the screen with shimmering pixels in green, yellow or red, indicating good, moderate or poor air quality both inside and out.
Tapping through to an “Air quality and pollen” screen gives more granular data, with various readings (nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, etc) displayed in micrograms per cubic metre, with a red-yellow-green rating for those of us who don’t know whether 47μg/m³ of ozone is good or bad (it’s OK, apparently). If the contaminants spike, the system temporarily stops bringing in external air and recirculates cabin air instead. Pollen levels are also listed; grass pollen topped the chart that day, but there were no watery, reddened eyes to be found inside the car.
If you’d like to step into a vehicle that’s already cleansed of contaminants (and cooled to your favoured temperature), that can be done remotely beforehand via the Polestar app. All this tech doesn’t make nasal sprays and eye drops redundant, but it did make that particular summer day a lot more comfortable.
Pure bliss
Sales of fans have been rocketing in the summer heat, and this one is notable for having a front-mounted camera that scans for people in the room and directs air towards each of them in turn (no image data leaves the machine, says Dyson). That’s a neat feature that works well, but its high-end air purification is perhaps more impressive, monitoring and removing pollutants including pollen, smoke, mould, formaldehyde and VOCs (volatile organic compounds). Readings are displayed on a small circular screen on the unit or in the Dyson app; auto mode takes care of reducing those readings to acceptable levels and pausing when its work is done. What it certainly doesn’t do – unlike cheap competitors – is merely push polluted air around a room.
Suck it and see
There are seven cylinder vacs in Miele’s Guard L1 range, but the “Allergy” model is the only one whose primary focus is the HEPA exhaust filter. That filter is designed to capture at least 99.9 per cent of airborne particles measuring 0.3 microns or larger from the vacuumed-up dust – including dust mite debris, pollen and pet dander – and then prevent them from emerging from the exhaust and back into the room. The HyClean dustbags used across the L1 range also play their part, neatly snapping shut as they’re removed to prevent the contents puffing into your face. My friend Sandra, a cleaner by profession, swears by Miele vacuums for visibly picking up dust and grime, but this filter’s retention of invisible allergens is equally heroic.
Sleep tight
Bedrooms would ideally provide some kind of sanctuary for allergy sufferers, but the wretched dust mite thrives in the warmth and humidity of mattresses and pillows. There’s a great deal of bedding out there that claims to have hypoallergenic qualities, but a critical attribute is that its material is woven tightly enough to stop mites slipping through. AllerGuard, developed in partnership with the Danish Asthma and Allergy Association, is a synthetic material designed to do just that, and while I winced slightly at the idea of synthetic bedding, this is breathable – no heat build-up, no sweating. This pack comprises pillow and mattress protectors along with a duvet and a portable storage bag – perfect for visits to hotels where mites may lurk.
Pet project
Conventional air purifiers struggle to do their job properly in homes with pets – having to vacuum fluff from their exterior is a common complaint – but the FP10 is designed to cope better with the hair and dander that can trigger allergic reactions. For starters, it’s a sizeable unit with decent suction power, pulling in more of the floating contaminants and trapping them inside. A motorised roller then actively cleans the filter, keeping pet hair in a dedicated, sealed collection bin that’s visible from the exterior – so, easily monitored, removed and emptied. This prolongs the life of the filter (two years before it needs replacing, say Dreame). A HEPA filter and UV light zap allergens and pathogens, while an active carbon filter helps absorb pet-related odours.

title: Ranking the Best Smart Glasses: Meta, Viture, & More (2026)
summary: This burgeoning wearable tech lets you talk to an AI assistant, listen to music, or check out a display screen from the comfort of your very own face.
full_text:
The Best Smart Glasses That Aren’t Just a Gimmick
Featured in this article
The idea of smart glasses has been around for decades, but the technology is finally catching up. The best smart glasses let you listen to music, answer texts hands-free, or teach you about the world, even as you're looking at it. And they're getting more popular: Meta and Ray-Ban sold more than 7 million pairs of smart glasses in 2025. Google, Samsung, and Apple are releasing their own versions soon. Even better than helpful smart glasses becoming more available is that these specs can also make you look fabulous.
Before you pick your pair, you should know that smart glasses are hugely varied, even more so than many other product categories that we test. Some are glorified headphones for everyday wear; others have very specific use cases, like for sports, gaming, or working. They also come in a wide variety of designs, with varying specs and price points.
The WIRED team has tested just about every pair of smart glasses on the market. In addition to our recommendations, I also explain what you need to know about this category and give a quick history lesson about the space. Think you might need something else instead? Don't forget to check out the rest of our buying guides, including the Best Meta Glasses and the Best Virtual Reality Headsets.
Updated August 2026: I updated product information and added a FAQ section. Specs, prices, and links were also updated.
What Am I Testing Next?
I am currently testing the Lucyd Reebok Optical frames.
Honorable Mentions
RayNeo Air 3s Pro for $299: TCL-owned RayNeo offers many models, and I've tested several. The latest Air 3s Pro glasses boast a 201-inch virtual screen (1080p, 120 Hz, 1200 nits), but the 46-degree field of view lets it down a little. Both color vibrancy and brightness are improved over previous releases like the Air 2s and the older TCL RayNeo Air 2 XR Glasses. You can just about see the whole screen clearly (even after adjusting, I had to slide them down my nose a little to avoid blurring at the bottom). You will also need the lens shade to use them in brighter environments. While they are cheaper than our other virtual-screen picks, I found them inferior in design, fit, and comfort. Rayneo has added some more on-device options, including spatial sound, but it didn't work well for me, though the standard sound is fine. RayNeo’s software, required for 3 DoF, is still buggy and unpolished. This is a good virtual screen for the money, and perfectly suitable for watching movies and light gaming, but if you want more from your smart glasses, I'd pick a different pair. —Simon Hill
Viture Luma Pro for $499: Every time a company comes out with a new pair of smart glasses, the old one instantly looks dated. The same is true here with the older Viture Luma Pro and the newer Viture Beast. The Beat's display is better, and it has the onboard chip, so you don't have to deal with the hassle of the SpaceWalker app. If you're using the glasses for gaming, you're probably going to spend whatever you save buying the older Luma Pro's on accessories anyway. That said, if you exhausted your budget, the Luma Pro is a cheaper way to get a small, portable screen for traveling. —Adrienne So
Engo3 for $400: These sports sunglasses are for high-performance aerobic athletes going at such high speeds that looking down at your wrist might place you in peril. The glasses are a miracle of engineering, weighing only 38.5 grams (half that of the Oakley Meta Vanguard). I tested the version with the photochromic lenses, which have an ambient light sensor to dial the transmittance up or down. You can connect the glasses with a compatible Garmin or Apple Watch and customize the HUD (heads-up display) to show real-time data on a color display as you're working out. It's accurate, and the text is crisp. Unfortunately, the HUD is located right near the bridge of my nose, which means I'm cross-eyed when I check it. Also, it's debatable which is more distracting during a long run: having to look down at my smartwatch or having a giant HUD mirrored display in the middle of my face, falling down my nose when I sweat. —Adrienne So
Chamelo Music Shield for $229: These are the simplest smart glasses on this list. If you're too cool for auto-transition photochromic lenses, you can just slide your finger along the right arm of these electrochromatic sunglasses to dim them anywhere from 17 to 64 percent light transmittance. They also play music. These are comfortable and work well, but the sound is nowhere near as clear or loud as other options. They're also not polarized and are pricey considering their limited functionality. —Adrienne So
Rokid Max 2 Glasses for $429: The Spider-Man–esque lenses give these comfortable smart glasses a bit of character, though they won’t be to everyone’s taste. They project a 215-inch screen (1080p, 120 Hz, 600 nits, 50-degree FoV) and have diopter dials for focus adjustments, but I struggled to eliminate blurring around the edges, and instead of using stylish electrochromic dimming, there’s a clip-on plastic blackout shield. I also tried the Rokid Station 2, which adds an Android TV interface to access entertainment apps, but also a trackpad and an air mouse for easier control. —Simon Hill
Lucyd Reebok Octane for $199: Designed in partnership with Reebok for cyclists and runners, these lightweight Bluetooth sunglasses feature silver polarized lenses, quality speakers, and an eight-hour battery life. I enjoyed listening to music and podcasts on them while hiking. I also like that you can hear the world around you, but the sound leakage isn’t too bad, so you won’t bother the people you pass. They also have physical controls that are much easier to use than touch controls, even when your hands are wet or sweaty (the glasses are water-resistant, too). You can take calls, get directions, and ask your preferred AI assistant questions. Lucyd has been making Bluetooth sunglasses for several years now and offers a wide range of different styles. We also tried the Lucyd 2.0 Bluetooth Sunglasses a couple of years ago, rating them a 7 out of 10. —Simon Hill
Avoid These Smart Glasses
Here's the eyewear that fell short.
Asus AirVision M1 for $699: I was excited to see Asus launch smart glasses, but the lack of fanfare was a red flag. My first impressions of the lightweight design were promising, and the M1 offers up to a 100-inch virtual display and impressive 1100 nits brightness. Designed to plug into your phone, laptop, PC, or handheld gaming device via USB-C, the M1 also features built-in speakers and a microphone. Sadly, the refresh rate maxes out at 72 Hz and is limited to 60 Hz unless you employ the Airvision software, which also enables you to select different modes (working, gaming, infinity), tweak screen position, and set interpupillary distance (IPD). I found the in-focus sweet spot was small, and most of my virtual screen was blurry, no matter how I tweaked the settings. This made the glasses uncomfortable to use, especially for work. There’s also a basic plastic shield to block light, rather than electrochromic dimming, and the speaker quality is decidedly average, leaving me puzzled about why the price is so high. —Simon Hill
Halliday Glasses: While these could almost pass for chunky regular glasses thanks to a clever ring controller and a tiny unobtrusive display, I can confidently say they are not the future of smart glasses. After spending several uncomfortable hours trying to adjust the display to be readable, all I got was a headache. The ring seemed like a smart idea, but it’s big, plastic, and laggy. The eavesdropping AI is slow, and squinting up to try and see the screens of unhelpful text it churns out is painful. The sound quality and battery life are likewise disappointing. —Simon Hill

title: The ‘Manosphere’ Isn’t a Movement. It’s a Multibillion-Dollar Grievance Industry
summary: Many young men are driven to resentment and are financially exploited as influencers sell them classes, pills, and the illusion of clout, a new report reveals.
full_text:
For many years now, a dark question has haunted parents, teachers, the internet, and media institutions: What’s wrong with young men?
Why, people ask, are boys so politically extreme, spouting misogynist rhetoric, and increasingly drawn into risky crypto schemes and online gambling? How did they become so lonely, with their depression symptoms often overlooked? The male youth vote broke for Trump in the 2024 election following a GOP campaign built on naked appeals to meathead machismo. Yet there are signs that his second term in office has done little to stem the anger of Gen Z men, whose support for the president is now plummeting.
The most common explanation of these interrelated phenomena is that younger men have banded together online under the umbrella of something known as the “manosphere,” usually conceived as an organic right-wing rebellion driving the culture wars. A new study, however, suggests that this is entirely backward: The digital ecosystem that produces red-pilled men is less of a movement than it is a pyramid scheme.
In “The Grift Economy: How Young Men Are Being Sold Fake Belonging and Fake Wealth Online,” researchers from the digital safety organization Reset Tech and the nonprofit Equimundo map how men are “algorithmically routed into paid communities, unregulated supplements, crypto schemes, and high-ticket ‘coaching’ programs,” which together make up a “multibillion-dollar industry.”
“‘Masculinity’ has become a commercial category that is constructed, curated, and financially incentivized online,” write the authors of the 153-page report.
First, men encounter aspirational self-help content when looking up advice on dating, fitness, or finance. Bad actors then exploit their areas of vulnerability by offering a misleading, grievance-based narrative to explain their frustrations. The paper cites, for example, a verified “business” account on X that used real economic data to falsely claim that the high rate of youth unemployment is only affecting men.
“By framing credential competition and labor market dynamics as a coordinated attack on men,” the researchers write, “this operation converts genuine economic anxiety—which is real and documented—into resentment with named targets: women, immigrants, foreign workers.”
Once men feel they are in community with one another based on a shared sense of victimhood and betrayal, and hostility toward a mutual enemy, the same predatory characters can then sell them the dubious solution, whether that’s a class, access to an exclusive club, or gray-market pills. In breaking down the sources of the misogynist influencer Andrew Tate’s income, the researchers estimate that he makes $184 million in annual gross revenue just from his subscription-based “Real World” education platform, which costs $99 per month. Reset Tech and Equimundo call these kinds of membership and course systems “fraud at scale,” noting their manipulative character: “Recycled content, affiliate pyramids, deliberate cancellation barriers, and deceptive testimonials characterize the industry’s flagship products.” (Tate’s attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Tate and his brother, Tristan Tate, are fighting extradition to the UK on charges of rape and sex trafficking after being arrested in Florida last month; their attorney has said they are innocent.)
Meanwhile, the report pegs the range of hourly streaming revenue for top-tier streamers such as Adin Ross (who also has an equity stake in Kick, the site that hosts his live content) at around $30,000 to $50,000. Figures like Joe Rogan command speaking fees upwards of $200,000. And top creators in the space, the study estimates, can earn anywhere from $1 million to $10 million in annual revenue across income streams including “platform payouts, sponsorships, courses, memberships, and speaking fees.” (Neither Rogan’s manager nor Ross’ entertainment company immediately returned a request for comment.)
Gary Barker, founder and CEO of Equimundo, which advocates for gender equality and positive masculinity, says we can better understand the so-called manosphere by looking at how those at the top are cultivating and then monetizing resentment and anger among young men. “They're being duped,” he says of these consumers. “They deserve to be getting straight information on products that actually do what they say they do, and not [be] swindled out of their money.”
The platforms, of course, take a cut of the profits and reward masculinity influencers for pushing extreme views while generating controversy and conflict. Reset Tech performed a cross-platform analysis of “looksmaxxing” content, heavily amplified this year by the Kick streamer Braden Peters, better known as Clavicular, to capture the scale of trends that drive men to pay exorbitant sums for the supposed means to improve their status. “Across 216 influencers tracked on TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, the combined reach of looksmaxxing-related operations exceeded 14.6 billion views during the analysis period,” they concluded. “The reach is not organic—it is a product of recommendation architecture.”
The report draws a parallel between this harmful material and the kind of pro-eating-disorder content that targets women. It notes that while platforms were eventually pressured to take action against the latter—though not always with success—they have not pursued the same kind of enforcement against users reinforcing men’s negative body image to promote unhealthy behaviors. (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, and Kick did not immediately respond to a request for comment on their guidelines around potentially harmful manosphere content.)
Clavicular’s rise to fame also provides evidence of how outrage fuels clicks that ultimately line the pockets of masculinity gurus. In January 2026, he and other influencers including Andrew and Tristan Tate, Nick Fuentes, and Sneako livestreamed themselves listening to Kanye West’s antisemitic song “Heil Hitler” in a sprinter van in Miami. Clips spread far beyond the original Kick audience via aggregator accounts on mainstream platforms, drawing widespread condemnation.
While the better-known Tates saw little change in their audience following the incident, Clavicular, who was then far less prominent, saw an explosion in engagement. Two weeks later, he was averaging close to 3 million views on his X posts, compared to about 500,000 two weeks before the stream. The larger viewership meant more potential students for his looksmaxxing “academy,” which costs $49 at the lowest tier and up to $3,000 for private coaching.
Barker says that while younger kids can be kept out of this pipeline by their parents, advocacy groups, and legislatively imposed protections, men entering adulthood don’t have the same support. “If we're looking at the 18- to 29-year-olds, which is where we see the biggest traffic to these spaces, nobody's got their back,” he says. This demographic “falls through the cracks” because society expects that they “should be able to handle this by themselves” as skeptical media consumers, he adds.
However, in post-2024 focus groups, Reset Tech found that young men could demonstrate a “striking lack of self-awareness” when it came to their sources of news and perspectives on current events, considering podcasts like The Joe Rogan Experience essentially unbiased. They also “believed women were trapped in echo chambers looking at makeup and lifestyle content while they themselves received information from neutral, verified sources,” the researchers write.

title: The Hottest New AI Chatbot Is Just a Guy Answering Your Questions
summary: WIRED spoke with Tucker Bryant, an artist and former Google employee who created ChatTJB to get people to reflect on the “strange moment” we’re in.
full_text:
What if, instead of typing the next silly question you have into Claude or ChatGPT, you asked a random guy instead?
That’s the idea behind ChatTJB. It’s the creation of 32-year-old Tucker Bryant, a public speaker, artist, and former project manager at Google. A San Francisco billboard describes ChatTJB as “the leading chat interface powered by AI.” In this case, though, AI stands for “average individual.”
Bryant didn’t train an LLM to respond based on how he writes. He literally sits down and answers the prompts himself. If you request an image of a skunk wearing sunglasses, he’ll scribble one up. If you ask how to fry an egg, he’ll respond with a suggestion. Maybe. (WIRED asked ChatTJB how to become a morning person, and at the time of writing, we haven’t received a response. The website notes that “thousands of people are writing in right now.”)
Bryant tells WIRED he launched ChatTJB back in April, but it didn’t take off until July 27, when his $6,000 billboard went up in San Francisco. News coverage soon followed. As of August 6, he says, ChatTJB has received over 30,000 queries. At its peak, he says, he was receiving about 5,000 prompts per hour.
Bryant says that he “first and foremost” considers ChatTJB to be an art project, not just a funny bit or a social experiment.
“It was sort of an opportunity for me to provide a little bit of commentary on a strange moment that I feel like we're in,” Bryant says. He doesn’t consider himself anti-AI—in fact, he vibe-coded the ChatTJB website using Lovable—but he’s clear-eyed about the risks of the technology.
He’s concerned about the risk of “cognitive surrender,” which refers to accepting AI outputs with increasingly little critical thinking or scrutiny. He says the concept made him reflect on his own back-and-forths with LLMs, like the time he asked if he should wear short or long sleeves on a 65-degree day in San Francisco.
“And then I'm like, dude, I've been living in this city for whatever, like seven years,” Bryant says. “Like, I know how to handle the weather. And yet, it felt like an easier thing for me to defer to a LLM for advice on that.”
“It felt like something that I wanted to speak on,” he adds, “because I was like, what am I doing here?”
Over the past couple of days, he has drawn a frog eating spaghetti, San Francisco mayor David Lurie as Godzilla, and two black cats eating grass on a table, among other things. The written requests, Bryant says, have been diverse.
“People were asking things like, ‘Oh, it's my birthday in two weeks, and I don't really want to have a party—what do you think I should do?’” Bryant says. Other people ask what they should have for dinner or how they can use the ingredients in their fridge.
“A lot of people initially were interacting with this thing as a joke or as a funny thing,” Bryant says. “And then I think when they realized that they could chat and get actual conversation, some of what people would share would be more personal, sincere, genuine, et cetera.”
Bryant is quick to note that he’s not a good artist, and his advice is no better than any other person’s. (On YouTube, he described it as “the worst LLM of all time.”) But he thinks people understand that.
“The way I'm interpreting it is that the value for them is just getting a human to bounce those questions off of, as opposed to getting super expert advice,” Bryant says. “It's very tender to see.”
At first, Bryant tells WIRED, he expected the project to last only a couple of days. But after seeing people’s enthusiasm, he says, he plans to keep it going. He has enlisted the help of 10 volunteers, but they’re a select crowd. Bryant says that over 3,000 people applied.
For ChatTJB superfans, there’s an option to financially support the project: ChatTJB Pro. Bryant is clear on the website that “this is a worthless tier,” and users get nothing but the knowledge that they’re supporting his art. So far, he says, about four people have paid the $5 per month fee—so he hasn’t exactly made up the cost of the billboard, which will remain up until late August. But Bryant says he didn’t create ChatTJB to make money.
“I really just want people to have an opportunity to take a second look at both their own relationship to technology as well as the world's relationship to technology,” Bryant says. He adds that in a time when people are bombarded with companies claiming to sell world-changing technology, alongside frightening coverage of a looming AI bubble, he wants to bring some levity.
“I hope that that just makes a weird time sit a little bit lighter,” Bryant says, “because I think sometimes that's the best that we can do.”

title: Ratio vs. Simply Good: Which Plastic-Free Coffee Maker Is Best?
summary: Microplastics are in everything, especially your coffee. A new generation of plastic-free drip coffee brewers is trying to change this.
full_text:
The era of plastic-free drip coffee has finally arrived. It couldn't come soon enough.
Drip coffee is my first true love when it comes to caffeine. But sadly, my first love is hopelessly addicted to plastic. From the very first Mr. Coffee machines in the 1970s, nearly every drip coffee maker on the market, including many of my favorite drip coffee makers, has included plastic at some point in the brewing process.
But plastic, as we're now learning, can leach tiny particles called microplastics into coffee or water, which you then happily drink in your morning cup. The science isn't all in on health risks, but it doesn't seem great.
Luckily, in the past year, a couple new machines have arrived with the promise to remove plastic from the equation: the Ratio Eight Series 2 ($799) and the Simply Good Coffee Plastic-Free Coffee Brewer ($480). Each promises to deliver delicious, high-end coffee without the plastic.
Each costs significantly more than machines made with injection-molded plastic parts that are easier to manufacture. And each has a couple quirks and trade-offs. But the Ratio Eight in particular makes drip coffee that rivals the best pour-over, and the best drip coffee I've ever tasted—and never brings hot water into contact with plastic.
But for those who want to avoid plastic completely, including on the cold water tank, there's really only one drip coffee maker I've tested that fits the bill: the Simply Good Coffee plastic-free brewer, which comes in at a much lower price.
If flavor is a primary consideration, I'd still recommend upgrading to the Ratio Eight. It's also the coffee maker that's become my daily driver when testing new coffee roasters and my favorite coffee subscriptions. But I understand that its price brings it out of reach for some. Here's the rundown.
The Fully Plastic-Free Machine: Simply Good Coffee
Simply Good Coffee is a fairly new name in the coffee world, founded in 2022 by former Bonavita CEO Laura Sommers. Until last year, it was also a reasonably obscure brand, devoted mostly to making more affordable takes on premium, precision coffee makers like the Bonavita and Moccamaster, whose design Simply Good Coffee somewhat resembles.
The plastic-free machine rocketed Simply Good into sudden prominence—and indeed, it's sold out its production runs more than once since its release last year, riding a wave of interest in plastic-free drip coffee makers. The design is similar to Simply Good's previous model, but with plastic parts removed from the equation.
The frame is made of 304 “food grade” stainless steel. The reservoir, carafe, and boiler tube are borosilicate glass. Certain connections, including the drip stop, are made with medical-grade, sand-based silicone fittings that are not thought to produce nanoparticles easily. It is, quite simply, the least plasticky drip coffee machine I am aware of. There's no plastic contact, hot or cold, and very minimal silicone contact.
Operation is dead simple. There are, in fact, just two switches. One turns on the brewer and the warming plate; the other controls the pour-over style “bloom” function, adding a small phase to wet the grounds before brewing a full batch. The machine will turn itself off after 40 minutes, or you can do so manually.
So how's the coffee? It's good. It's generally light-bodied, brewing in six minutes even on full 40-ounce batches. It's tested, but not certified, to maintain precise brewing temperatures throughout the entire brewing process. The results are better than most basic drip coffee makers, but don't quite keep pace with the best-of-the-best coffee makers: the Moccamasters, the Fellows, the Ratios. There's a coffee warmer, which I don't prefer, but many do.
Some parts aren't machined as precisely as I'd hope, leading to a little jiggle or awkward fits. And customer service is also a lesser-known quantity with Simply Good. Calls to the customer service center during business hours reached only AI operators. But I did receive a call back a couple days later from someone I believe to be human. And the replacement warranty is an excellent five years.
In the end, if you're buying this, you're buying it because, for now, it is the drip coffee maker that is the most dedicated to ensuring that your coffee maker isn't adding microplastics to your cup. If you filter your water for microplastics, the Simply Good Coffee will likely not add any microplastics after the fact. That's a lot of peace of mind.
Coffee Flavor
The Simply Good Coffee brewer, like the Moccamaster it resembles, has been tested for compliance with “Golden Cup” parameters laid out by the Specialty Coffee Association, designed to describe best coffee brewing practices.
These include, but aren't limited to, the ability to keep coffee within tight time and temperature parameters while brewing—specifically, between 92 and 96 degrees Celsius. Each batch also remains within optimum times, brewing even a full batch in about six minutes. Simply Good received independent lab testing showing its capability to stay within tight brewing parameters. But it did not go through the far more rigorous and expensive SCA certification process.
This effort places Simply Good squarely in the “premium” category, and the coffee is going to taste better than most standard drip machines whose temperature can range wildly over the course of the brewing process. However, while the coffee tastes good, it doesn't taste as good as the Ratio—nor any of my other top drip coffee maker picks.
I noted some trouble with wetting coffee grounds evenly, especially on full 40-ounce batches, which can lead to under-extraction in some places and over-extraction in others. Which is to say: less precision of flavor, and a certain flatness. I didn't detect off notes, but I've also never had a cup with the Simply Good that I've been extremely excited about. And I've brewed dozens of batches.
Note that the warming plate gets quite warm, and it stays on during the brewing process, which means the coffee gets overheated during the early phases of brewing, leading to a small bit of diner-coffee oxidation in every batch—even if you take the carafe off after the batch completes.
Most coffee drinkers won't notice these quibbles much. But aficionados will. And among high-end coffee makers topping $400, Simply Good quite simply does not taste as good.
Flavor: 7/10
Ease of Use and Cleaning
Like the Moccamaster it resembles, the Simply Good machine has almost no buttons. Its operation is mostly as simple as turning it off and on, and choosing whether you'd like a “bloom” function that mimics pour-over.
But also like the Moccamaster, there are a lot of little parts: a reservoir lid, a shower attachment, a detachable brew chamber, a top for the chamber, a carafe with a detachable lid. Not all of these fit perfectly, or comfortably. The showerhead attachment has a little wobble to it.
The lid to the carafe can grind a bit, metal on glass, if you put it on even slightly crookedly—an uncomfortable form of friction that makes me worry about longevity. More parts also means more parts to clean. And while they can be put in the dishwasher, I doubt you'll do so daily.
The drip stop is both helpful and a potential hazard, depending on who you are. If you don't use the drip stop, there'll be a bit of dripping after the main brew. But if you do, there's a risk you won't notice it's still activated when you go to brew a batch. This'll cause an overflow if you let it. Entirely user error. And yet I've done it more than once.
Still, simple is simple. And it's dead simple to use, and hard to screw up. And stainless steel and borosilicate glass both clean quite easily.
Ease: 7/10
Best Upgrade Plastic-Free Coffee Maker: Ratio Eight

title: Ondo Finance Founder’s Mother Sues in Delaware to Take Control and Remove CEO Ian De Bode
summary:
Kathleen Allman says Ian De Bode declared himself CEO without board approval after her son's death, and asks a Delaware judge to confirm she controls Ondo.

The post Ondo Finance Founder’s Mother Sues in Delaware to Take Control and Remove CEO Ian De Bode appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
A corporate control fight has broken out at tokenized real-world asset issuer Ondo Finance, with the mother of founder Nathan Allman accusing former president and current CEO Ian De Bode of improperly seizing control of the company after Allman’s death in May, The Block first reported Thursday.
Allman died as Ondo’s CEO, sole director and controlling shareholder, leaving the board with no sitting directors and his voting power locked inside his estate, Kathleen Allman was quoted as saying in the filings by CoinDesk. She was appointed personal representative by a Hawaii probate court on June 26.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
ONDO, the native token of Ondo, carries a market value near $2 billion, and the company is one of the largest issuers in real-world asset tokenization, with products including the USDY and OUSG tokens. The estate is seeking an expedited ruling on the grounds that uncertainty over who runs the company could affect contracts, spending and equity issuances.
The complaint says De Bode claimed he automatically became CEO under Ondo’s bylaws without board action, installed himself as sole director through a voting agreement, and began hiring advisors and approving performance grants, according to the reports. Allman reportedly said she initially sought a cooperative transition, reaffirming De Bode as president, but alleges the company refused to recognize her authority or hand over a shareholder list. She expanded the board and appointed Gordon Liao, who declined, and Tahnee Towill, Nathan Allman’s sister. On July 24, the two voted to remove De Bode from all positions and installed Allman as chair and interim CEO.
De Bode reportedly said Allman’s claims are “meritless” and that Ondo retains the support of its lead investors and the Ondo Foundation, calling the lawsuit not in the interests of the company or its stockholders.
Nathan Allman founded Ondo in 2021 after leaving Goldman Sachs, raising $20 million in a 2022 Series A backed by Founders Fund and Pantera Capital. The SEC closed a two-year investigation into the firm without charges in December.

title: Volunteer Red Team Says AI Audit Turned Up 85 Critical Bugs Across 390 Bitcoin Projects

This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.

The group, which calls itself the Bitcoin Red Team, at the roughly 27-hour mark was averaging 2.31 high or critical findings per person per hour, Calle said, adding that the rate was climbing as the team’s automated harnesses improved.
The disclosure volume has created a second problem. Calle apologized to maintainers overwhelmed by reports and said the team is still learning to separate real findings from noise, while saying that fast publication was necessary because others could find the same bugs. The audit comes after the Coldcard hardware wallet exploit. Coldcard sweeps that began July 30 have drained over $100 million from user wallets. AI-driven discovery has already reshaped crypto security elsewhere: an AI-assisted audit of Zcash in June found a bug that could have minted unlimited counterfeit ZEC .

“The Dems are insistent on no Clarity vote,” the spokesperson said on X. “I worked with sponsors of the bill. [Sen. Cynthia Lummis] was great, and we’re getting that queued up first thing when we come back.”

full_text:
宇樹科技董事長王興興 8 月 7 日在網上投資者交流會上表示，公司與 DeepSeek 已簽署戰略合作備忘錄，雙方將在通用人工智慧研發、高效能通用機器人與 AI 大模型三個方向重點合作。前一天揭露的策略配售名單顯示，DeepSeek 認購 933,399 股、約 1.41 億元人民幣，閉鎖期 36 個月，是大模型公司第一次以股東身分綁進人形機器人廠。
（前情提要：人形機器人第一股》宇樹科技科創板定價 150.8 元，估「中一籤狂賺 17 萬」）
（背景補充：宇樹科技 IPO 時間表確定，上市日期、估值與投資者需要知道的一切）
重點摘要
- 王興興在 8 月 7 日網上路演證實，宇樹與 DeepSeek 已簽戰略合作備忘錄，鎖定通用人工智慧、高效能通用機器人、AI 大模型三個方向
- DeepSeek 以 933,399 股、約 1.41 億元人民幣進入策略配售名單，閉鎖 36 個月，騰訊旗下投資公司認購約 1.36 億元
- 公告揭露的合作條款是雙向的「同等條件下優先」，宇樹優先用 DeepSeek 的模型服務，DeepSeek 優先買宇樹的機器人
宇樹科技（Unitree）董事長王興興週五（8/7）在網上投資者交流會上說，公司已經和 DeepSeek 簽下戰略合作備忘錄，兩邊會在通用人工智慧研發、高效能通用機器人、AI 大模型這三個方向重點合作。
這句話的時間點抓得很準。就在前一天，宇樹才公布科創板 IPO 的策略配售名單，DeepSeek 的名字第一次出現在上面。
錢先到位
按照 8 月 6 日的公告，宇樹這次策略配售共有 9 家投資人，合計拿下 808.9 萬股，佔發行總量的 20%。其中杭州深度求索人工智慧基礎技術研究公司，也就是 DeepSeek 的營運主體，認購 933,399 股，以每股 150.80 元人民幣的發行價計算約 1.41 億元人民幣，閉鎖期 36 個月。
騰訊旗下投資公司拿下 903,290 股、約 1.36 億元人民幣，中石油旗下崑崙資本、南方電網財務控股、中國電信資本控股也在名單上，配售金額同樣落在 1.3 億元人民幣上下。宇樹在公告裡把這批投資人定義為「與發行人具有戰略合作關係或長期合作願景的大型企業」。
中國 AI 圈是第一次出現入股人形機器人廠的股東名單。DeepSeek 過去幾乎不做對外投資，這次不但出手，還選了閉鎖期最長的那檔。
協議寫的是同等條件下優先
比三個合作方向更具體的，是公告揭露的協議條款。雙方談定的是一組雙向安排：宇樹在採購模型訓練服務與技術方案時，同等條件下優先選擇 DeepSeek；DeepSeek 在採購機器人或探索具身智慧應用時，同等條件下優先選擇宇樹。
「同等條件下」這五個字是重點。這是一份意向性的優先權，不是排他協議，也沒有約定採購金額或數量。換句話說，如果哪天有別家模型跑得更快更便宜，宇樹並沒有被綁死；反過來也一樣。這種寫法在 A 股的策略配售協議裡很常見，它確保雙方有正式的合作名分，但保留了各自的退路。
王興興的雙軌路線
同一場路演裡，王興興還講了一件外界比較少注意的事，宇樹的具身大模型是兩條路線並行的。一條是 WMA 世界模型，另一條是 VLA 視覺、語言、動作具身大模型，兩邊都已經開源出成果，UnifoLM-WMA-0 在 2025 年 9 月釋出、UnifoLM-VLA-0 在 2026 年 1 月釋出，這次募資的專案也會讓兩條線繼續並行。
零組件策略同樣是兩部分，包括機器人身體結構、運動控制系統、關節模組這些牽動效能的核心模組留在自家研發，其餘品項多、規格散的功能件則走外部採購，用來應付客戶的各種需求。至於產品形態，王興興說會繼續往人形機器人、四足機器人、外骨骼甚至機甲探索。
財務數字是這輪敘事的底氣。宇樹 2023 到 2025 年的營收分別是 1.59 億、3.93 億與 16.99 億元人民幣，歸母淨利從 2023 年虧損 1.11 億元轉為 2024 年賺 9,450 萬元、2025 年賺 2.78 億元，是全球少數做到規模化出貨又能獲利的機器人公司。以 150.80 元的發行價計算，上市後市值約 610 億元人民幣。
這也是為什麼 DeepSeek 這 1.41 億元人民幣看起來不像一筆財務投資。它買的不是報酬率，是一台已經有出貨量的機器人業務，以及未來三年都不能中途退場的位置。
常見問題
DeepSeek 在宇樹的策略配售裡認購了多少？
933,399 股，以發行價每股 150.80 元人民幣計算約 1.41 億元人民幣，閉鎖期 36 個月，是本次 9 家策略投資人中閉鎖期最長的一檔。騰訊旗下投資公司認購 903,290 股、約 1.36 億元人民幣。
兩家公司實際上約定了什麼？
公告揭露的是雙向的優先權條款：宇樹採購模型訓練服務與技術方案時，同等條件下優先選 DeepSeek；DeepSeek 採購機器人或探索具身智慧應用時，同等條件下優先選宇樹。條款沒有約定採購金額或數量，也不具排他性。

title: Coldcard 漏洞引起恐慌，12 萬枚 BTC 轉移錢包地址！但只有一成進交易所
summary:
Coldcard 硬體錢包的種子漏洞在鏈上留下了規模驚人的痕跡。Glassnode 數據顯示，7 月 31 日 […]

〈Coldcard 漏洞引起恐慌，12 萬枚 BTC 轉移錢包地址！但只有一成進交易所〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Coldcard 硬體錢包的種子漏洞在鏈上留下了規模驚人的痕跡。Glassnode 數據顯示，7 月 31 日盜竊發生後三天內，約 11.9 萬枚沉睡超過一年的比特幣被移動，是被盜量（594 枚）的 200 倍，成為本輪週期規模最大的老幣被迫遷移。但只有約十分之一流向交易所，其餘搬進了全新的冷錢包，現貨市場幾乎沒有反應。
（前情提要：比特幣活躍地址創 2024 年來新高！Glassnode：Coldcard 漏洞引發「恐慌性轉移」）
（背景補充：Coldcard MK3 冷錢包爆「種子漏洞」：594 枚比特幣 25 分鐘掃空，官方籲用戶盡速遷移資產）
重點摘要
- Glassnode：Coldcard 事件後三天約 11.9 萬枚休眠一年以上的比特幣被移動
- 遷移規模是被盜 594 枚比特幣的 200 倍，僅約十分之一流入交易所
- 成立不到一個月的新錢包持有的比特幣供給量，事件後增加 40%
被偷走 594 枚，跑了 11.9 萬枚。鏈上分析商 Glassnode 在最新一期週報中揭露，7 月 31 日 Coldcard 種子漏洞遭利用之後的三天內，約有 11.9 萬枚沉睡超過一年的比特幣被喚醒移動，規模是被盜量的 200 倍。
這個數字來自 Glassnode 的「Revived Supply 1y+」指標，白話說就是統計那些至少 12 個月沒動過、突然被轉出的幣。平常這條線很平，因為長期持有者不常動作，一旦拉高通常代表有人在賣。這次不是。
Glassnode 把這次定調為本輪週期規模最大的老幣被迫移動潮。被迫兩個字是重點，這些人本來沒打算動，是漏洞逼著他們動。
錢沒去交易所，去了新錢包
最能說明性質的是資金去向，Glassnode 統計，這波被喚醒的幣裡只有大約十分之一流入交易所，其餘都轉進了新地址。
另個指標更直接，成立不到一個月的錢包所持有的比特幣供給量，在事件後增加了 40%，而且還在往上爬。錢不是拿去賣，是換了個保險箱。
市場的反應也印證了這點，Glassnode 在報告裡寫，現貨市場「幾乎沒有察覺這件事」，沒有可測量的賣壓，也沒有明顯的價格反應。十幾萬枚老幣同時移動卻沒有砸盤，這在鏈上數據裡是很少見的組合。
換韌體救不了已經生成的種子
要理解為什麼鏈上動作這麼大，得回到漏洞本身。
問題出在 2021 年 3 月的一次韌體整合失誤，裝置在產生種子時，本該呼叫 STM32 晶片內建的硬體亂數產生器，卻被導向一個軟體的偽亂數產生器，等於把應該無法預測的隨機性，換成了可以推算的程式輸出。攻擊者因此得以反推出私鑰，直接在鏈上把幣轉走。
受影響的範圍包括在韌體 4.0.1 之後設定的部分 Mk3 裝置，以及使用舊韌體的 Mk4、Mk5 與 Q 系列。
Coinkite 在 7 月 31 日對所有受影響機型發布了緊急韌體，但關鍵在於，更新韌體不會修好已經生成的種子。官方的說法是，種子有疑慮的用戶必須在更新後的裝置上重新產生一組新種子，再把幣搬過去。這就是 11.9 萬枚老幣為什麼會在三天內集體上路。
至於損失規模，鏈上分析商 TRM Labs 統計攻擊分四波進行，超過 5,200 個地址被掃空，累計約 1,816 枚比特幣、約 1.16 億美元。各家估計值從 8,900 萬到 1.3 億美元不等，差異來自統計的時間點不同。Coinkite 到 8 月 6 日為止仍拒絕估算損失金額。
常見問題
Coldcard 漏洞造成多少比特幣損失？
鏈上分析商 TRM Labs 統計，攻擊分四波進行，超過 5,200 個地址遭掃空，累計約 1,816 枚比特幣、約 1.16 億美元。各家估計從 8,900 萬到 1.3 億美元不等，差異來自統計時點。Coinkite 至今拒絕估算損失。
用 Coldcard 的人現在該做什麼？
Coinkite 已於 7 月 31 日對所有受影響機型發布緊急韌體，但更新韌體不會修復已經生成的種子。2021 年 3 月之後在受影響韌體上產生種子的用戶，必須在更新後的裝置重新產生新種子，並把資產轉到新地址。
動區昨日報導，比特幣每日活躍地址在這波遷移中衝上 98 萬個，創下 2024 年 12 月以來新高。把兩組數據疊起來看，這次事件在鏈上留下的最終紀錄不是價格，是十幾萬枚老幣換了新住址。

title: Wintermute 在美註冊為「經紀自營商」，將跨足股票、選擇權與加密 ETF 交易
summary:
加密貨幣做市商 Wintermute 宣布，旗下子公司已向美國證管會（SEC）及美國金融業監管局（FINRA）註冊為「經紀自營商（Broker-Dealer）」，未來將擴大業務版圖，進軍股票、選擇權、大宗商品及加密貨幣 ETF 交易，進一步推動傳統金融（TradFi）與數位資產市場融合。

〈Wintermute 在美註冊為「經紀自營商」，將跨足股票、選擇權與加密 ETF 交易〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
加密貨幣做市商 Wintermute 正式跨足傳統金融市場。該公司周四宣布，旗下子公司已向美國證管會（SEC）及美國金融業監管局（FINRA）註冊為「經紀自營商（Broker-Dealer）」，未來將擴大業務版圖，進軍股票、選擇權、大宗商品及加密貨幣 ETF 交易，進一步推動傳統金融（TradFi）與數位資產市場融合。
Wintermute 表示，取得券商資格後，公司可為美國證券交易所及場外交易（OTC）市場提供流動性，也能透過自營帳戶（Proprietary Trading）交易股票與選擇權。此外，公司還可自行辦理數位資產證券的結算業務，並擔任 ETF 的授權參與者。
所謂「經紀自營商（Broker-Dealer）」，是指同時具備「經紀商（Broker）」與「自營商（Dealer）」資格的金融機構，須取得 SEC 與 FINRA 註冊，既能代表客戶執行證券交易，也能使用自有資金進行投資與做市交易。
另一項重要資格則是授權參與者（Authorized Participant，AP）。 AP 是 ETF 生態系中的核心角色，負責透過申購與贖回基金單位來維持 ETF 市價與淨值平價，也是 ETF 流動性的重要提供者。
隨著 Wintermute 取得這兩項資格，公司未來將可更深入參與美國 ETF 市場，尤其是快速成長的加密貨幣 ETF 領域。
Wintermute 創辦人、執行長 Evgeny Gaevoy 表示：「我們始終相信，數位資產市場的發展絕對不會只有單一方向。傳統金融與數位資產將持續並行發展，在更多場景中相互交會，最終實現更深層次的融合。」
Wintermute 也表示，這次跨足傳統金融市場，正值資產代幣化快速發展之際，而儘管 SEC 近年對區塊鏈創新持較開放態度，也積極鼓勵市場探索資產代幣化應用，但監管立場依舊明確。
SEC 多次強調，證券代幣化並不代表可以豁免既有證券法規，凡涉及鏈上證券交易、發行或相關服務，仍須依法取得相應執照及監管資格。
事實上，Wintermute 近來持續拓展業務範圍，先是年初宣布進軍代幣化黃金市場，提供機構級做市服務；隨後又進一步將交易基礎設施延伸至預測市場，為相關平台提供雙向流動性。
總部位於倫敦的 Wintermute 表示，目前每日平均交易量已超過 100 億美元，並在全球超過 60 家中心化交易所（CEX）與去中心化交易所（DEX）提供流動性服務。新成立的 Wintermute USA 則將設立於紐約，作為拓展美國市場的重要據點。

title: I was standing in front of my teacher when she was shot, Thai pupil says
summary: The student says she had to climb over a school fence to flee the shooting which killed five teachers.
full_text:
I was standing in front of my teacher when she was shot, Thai pupil says
- Published
On Friday morning, as the final classes of the week were under way, panicked students began streaming out of a prestigious school just outside Bangkok.
Inside, police say, a 14-year-old boy had opened fire.
"I was standing in front of the teacher when she was shot," a shaken seventh grader tells the BBC, near the gates of Debsirin School in Nonthaburi. "She was talking to me when [the gunman] showed up."
Still in her uniform, with her mother by her side, she explains how the shooter stalked from room to room.
Authorities say he killed five teachers and injured more than 30 people - including fellow pupils - before turning the weapon on himself. Earlier, he had gunned down his grandparents.
"I had to climb over the school fence to escape with other friends," the girl, who the BBC is not naming, continues.
Her mother says the girl thought she might die. "[She said] 'I thought I'd never see you again'."
One 18-year-old student told Reuters he initially thought firecrackers were going off.
"I didn't think it was a gun at first," he said. "There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."
Metres from the school gates, paramedics loaded the wounded into ambulances and rushed them to hospital, as milling crowds hugged and cried.
Rescue worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith rushed to the scene after hearing children as young as 12 had been shot.
"I saw students who had been shot, some in the arm, some in the back, some in the chest. So I rushed to help get them to the hospital first," the 47-year-old rescue worker told Reuters news agency.
One grieving teacher told the BBC one of his friends was among the dead.
"She was my age. We went to this school together as students. Then we both became teachers at this school," the 31-year-old, who declined to give his name, said.
It is early days in the investigation and police haven't said anything about a motive.
They believe the 9mm handgun the shooter used belonged to his grandfather, who was a teacher. Forensic officers found the gunman's shots to be "quite accurate", with several hitting "vital spots" on victims' bodies.
Others are filling some of the gaps. A teacher at the school has said the shooter was a good student - not aggressive and with good grades - and education authorities have described him as an avid gamer.
But it is clear authorities will have many questions to answer in the coming days - many of them about what change this crime must trigger.
Renewed calls for gun control reform
This is Thailand's deadliest mass shooting in years - and the second at a school this year.
In February, a head teacher and a female student were shot by an 18-year-old gunman during a school siege in southern Thailand.
Four years ago, a 34-year-old in the eastern Nong Bua Lamphu province killed 37 people, most of them preschoolers, in a shooting and stabbing at a nursery.
These crimes have resurfaced questions about gun control in the country.
"This shouldn't have happened," the boyfriend of one of the killed teachers told reporters, clearly distressed and trying to hold back tears.
More than seven million people are believed to own guns in the country, one of the highest rates of ownership in the world. Of those, more than one million are unlicensed owners.
While there are restrictions on gun licences in Thailand, people can still acquire the weapons - legally or illegally - with relative ease.
There is a thriving black market, aided by Thailand's porous land borders with four other nations. Problems with corruption and loose regulation in the police and military have seen weapons end up in the wrong hands.
In response to the Friday's shooting, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he had tightened regulations when he was interior minister three years ago - suspending new gun permits.
But gun crime remains rife, with deaths from gunshots among the highest in the region. And some in the community are calling for greater action.
"An act of violence in an educational institution, which should be one of the safest places in our society, serves as a stark reminder for Thai society to seriously and systematically review gun control measures," Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut, leader of the People's Party - an opposition party - wrote in a Facebook post.

title: England footballer Ivan Toney charged with assault at Soho nightclub
summary: The 30-year-old former Brentford striker is due to appear in court next month.
full_text:
England footballer Toney charged with assault in Soho
- Published
England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault at a nightclub in central London.
The 30-year-old, who plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, was charged on 31 July following an incident on Wardour Street in Soho on 6 December.
The former Brentford striker, who started England's 6-4 win over France in the "bronze final" of the World Cup last month, has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm and is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 24 September.
A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."
After starting his career at Northampton Town, the striker had permanent spells at Newcastle, Peterborough and Brentford before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2024.
He was a surprise selection for England's World Cup squad but apart from the France game, his only other appearance was as a late substitute in the 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

title: NHS Tayside investigates data breach into Minnie Merriman medical records
summary: Minnie Merriman, from West Yorkshire, died at Ninewells Hospital in Dundee after being found seriously injured at an industrial estate in the town.
full_text:
NHS Tayside investigates data breach into Minnie Merriman medical records
- Published
NHS Tayside is investigating an alleged data breach into the medical records of a nine-year-old girl at the centre of a murder probe in Arbroath.
Minnie Merriman, from West Yorkshire, died at Ninewells Hospital in Dundee after being found seriously injured at an industrial estate in the town.
A 35-year-old man, who was known to the girl, has appeared in court charged with her murder.
NHS Tayside said it was "investigating the circumstances" of the alleged breach that happened in a clinical area where staff access patient information.
A spokesperson added : "As a matter of governance, any data protection breach would be recorded and investigated by NHS Tayside and, where appropriate, reported to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).
"It would not be appropriate for us to comment further on individual staffing matters."
Officers had been called to the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath shortly after midnight on Monday.
Police said they were not looking for anyone else in connection with Minnie's death and the other members of the family - who were camping in the area - are being supported by specialist officers.
Christopher Rice from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, made no plea during an appearance in private at Forfar Sheriff Court on Wednesday and was remanded in custody.
In a statement Minnie's family said: "We are devastated with the loss of our beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo.
"Our family asks that our privacy is respected at this extremely difficult time."
